faults.name: rx_crc_skips_first_byte
faults.why: the FCS check is computed over one byte too few (the brief's example)

faults.name: rx_ends_on_first_low_crs_dv
faults.why: CRS_DV toggling at the end of a frame is taken as the end of the frame

faults.name: rx_runt_not_flagged
faults.why: frames shorter than 64 bytes pass as good

faults.name: tx_pad_fcs_not_inverted
faults.why: padded frames go out with the wrong first FCS byte

faults.name: tx_short_ifg
faults.why: the inter-frame gap is one byte time short

faults.name: no_learning
faults.why: source addresses are never learnt, so everything floods

faults.name: flood_back_to_ingress
faults.why: floods go back out of the port they came in on

faults.name: no_ingress_vlan_filter
faults.why: a port outside the VLAN can inject into it

faults.name: stash_never_searched
faults.why: the hash-collision path (keys in the stash) is never looked up (the brief's example)

faults.name: bank1_never_used
faults.why: a key whose bank-0 bucket is taken is reported inserted but never written

faults.name: age_removes_used
faults.why: the AGE sweep removes recently used entries too

faults.name: best_match_not_kept
faults.why: a shorter prefix found higher in the trie is forgotten when a deeper level has no route

faults.name: wrong_key_byte_level2
faults.why: level 2 is indexed by the wrong address byte

faults.name: highest_index_wins
faults.why: overlapping rules resolve to the wrong one

faults.name: care_mask_ignored
faults.why: every bit is compared (no wildcards)

faults.name: action_written_early
faults.why: the new action is visible while a lookup that matched the old rule is still in flight (a race found and fixed in this brief)

faults.name: ipv4_options_ignored
faults.why: the IPv4 header is taken as 20 bytes whatever the IHL (the brief's example)

faults.name: csum_carry_dropped
faults.why: the ones' complement end-around carry is lost

faults.name: one_vlan_tag_only
faults.why: the inner tag of a double-tagged frame is taken as the EtherType

faults.name: fragment_offset_ignored
faults.why: non-first fragments report payload bytes as ports

faults.name: truncation_not_flagged
faults.why: a frame that ends inside a header is not marked

faults.name: overflow_not_counted
faults.why: packets dropped on a full queue are not counted (the brief's example)

faults.name: drr_no_subtract
faults.why: DRR never charges a queue for what it sent

faults.name: strict_priority_inverted
faults.why: the highest-numbered queue is served first

faults.name: space_freed_early
faults.why: a full region is overwritten instead of dropping the packet

faults.name: rfc1624_without_complement
faults.why: the incremental update adds the deltas to the checksum itself rather than to its complement

faults.name: udp_zero_checksum_rewritten
faults.why: a UDP datagram sent without a checksum gets one (RFC 768 says leave zero)

faults.name: pop_loses_tlast
faults.why: a frame that ends inside the popped tag loses its end (a bug found and fixed in this brief)
